comment_language: Some grammatical errors eg this personalised voice assistant 'are' ... and everyone of us 'have' it ...
comment_vocal_pronunciation: Some words could be pronounced more clearly.  Some tendency to slur or string words together when speaking eg how many of us 'recognise this logo'?
comment_vocal_volume_pace: Mostly confident and enthusiastic. Slight hesitations when explaining the slide on Multitask Learning.
comment_vocal_fluency: Mostly fluent with some use of fillers 'er' for some parts of the presentation eg when trying to explain the research gap leading to Multitask Learning.
comment_nonvocal: Consistently engages audience with appropriate eye contact and purposeful gestures eg uses a 'pointing gesture' when giving an example of Timmy pointing at an apple
comment_visuals_design: The presenter uses clear and attractive slides that help to enhance the audience's understanding of the content and main ideas.
comment_visuals_techniques_sync: The presenter synchronises his explanation and words effectively with the visuals eg he shows the logo for Shazam and talks about Shazam
comment_visuals_techniques_reference: The presenter constantly refers the audience to his visuals as he speaks, eg he points to the Shazam logo on his slide and he uses an arrow on PPT to direct audience to the examples of apple and orange.
overall_comment: A strong, effective presenter — communicates the research clearly with confidence, and visuals are well integrated with the speech. Minor refinements would polish an already competent academic talk.

comment_language: Besides the repetition of "so", the grammar is accurate and language is understood.
comment_vocal_pronunciation: Due to L1 interference, many words are not clear. I had to play the video more than 3 times to discern his speech at word and sentence level.
comment_vocal_volume_pace: Falls short on volume - he was too soft and I had to strain to hear him. Pace is generally sound.
comment_vocal_fluency: His pause is to say "so"  very often. Although it does not impede understanding, it is a habit that needs to be gotten rid of to achieve greater fluency.
comment_nonvocal: Became better in the second half of the speech although he started very tentatively in engaging the audience through insufficient eye contact especially.
comment_visuals_design: Mostly understood though one may question the necessity of the "Jackie Chan" slide as it does not seem to serve a purpose for clarity.
comment_visuals_techniques_sync: Yes, mostly in sync. However, when explaining the technology, could use the words on the slides more. He seemed to want to explain it in his own words but it makes the listener feel that we need to decode the explanations on the slides ourselves.
comment_visuals_techniques_reference: He does ask the audience sometimes to look at the slides. However, he should use signal words more liberally.
overall_comment: An adequate presenter — the core ideas come across, but several dimensions (clarity, delivery, or visuals) have noticeable weaknesses that limit the overall impact of the academic communication.

comment_language: Some errors in grammar/ phrasing of sentences eg Can this framework can truly adapt to ...and three 'step'.

comment_vocal_volume_pace: The presenter could try to sound more confident and enthusiastic.  He seems to be reading from his notes and he may tend to sound monotonous after a while.

comment_nonvocal: Limited eye contact and use of gestures.  The presenter could engage the audience with more widely directed and sustained eye contact.  Some inappropriate gesture eg arm over the stomach/ waist.

comment_visuals_techniques_sync: The presenter could synchronise his speech more clearly with the content for some slides for eg slide on Proposal:  Multimodal Emotion Extraction.
comment_visuals_techniques_reference: The presenter demonstrates some appropriate attempt to direct his audience to his visuals for eg when he explains the Multimodal EmoTTS Framework Overview. However, he could use more verbal signposts and gestures for other slides.
overall_comment: An adequate presenter — the core ideas come across, but several dimensions (clarity, delivery, or visuals) have noticeable weaknesses that limit the overall impact of the academic communication.

comment_language: Errors discerned both in speech and slides. Slide 2 (after introduction slide) contains grammatical/sentence structure errors - it is unclear what "which" refers to . In speech, there are singular-plural mistakes, amongst others.
comment_vocal_pronunciation: Though pronunciation is understood, his enunciation needs polish. He tends to trail off at the ends of sentences.
comment_vocal_volume_pace: Volume could be increased. Voice does not convey passion or enthusiasm. Voice is rather monotonous.
comment_vocal_fluency: Some "ums" but still generally fine for fluency as there were virtually no inappropriate pauses.
comment_nonvocal: Speaker rarely engages the audience. No eye contact with them, mostly looking at the monitor or screen. No gestures.
comment_visuals_design: Slides on the VITS Architecture are cluttered and unclear. Even the speaker admitted that they "look complicated". He could represent the concepts more clearly.
comment_visuals_techniques_sync: Generally in sync though he may not have explained everything on each slide since some slides had too much information.
comment_visuals_techniques_reference: Speaker does not really draw attention to the important content of his visuals, even signaling that his slides "look complicated". He should use appropriate signal words to guide the audience through his visuals.
overall_comment: A developing presenter — meaningful gaps across multiple dimensions interfere with the audience's understanding. Targeted coaching is needed before this would meet expectations for an academic talk.
